1. The post copy

League City answers on November 3rd.

In 2023 the Legislature added $1 to Texans' auto insurance. A state agency turned the fee into at least 3,200 Flock cameras. In late August the Governor ordered the funding paused. It came as scrutiny over the "AI-powered surveillance devices" mounted, the Tribune reported.

At least 14 cities and counties have since shut off more than 900 Flock cameras, the Tribune reported. El Paso voted on a 60 day clock for its fixed Flock cameras and passed it as revised. Leander stopped "in response to community concerns". Kyle kept its contract 6 to 1. College Station kept its cameras 4 to 2. Laredo asks voters in May.

League City called a nonbinding vote on August 11th, before the pause. Its ballot asks if police should keep the fixed cameras. What will a voter who drives past one say on November 3rd?

#LeagueCity #FlockSafety #ElPaso

    All three judges named the blank green sign faces in all five rounds. The reader judge named this fix in rounds 4 and 5. Proved on scratch copies of frames 1, 2 and 4 with the accent gate held over its floor. Commit 11db5c0.

    Round 5's top ranked artwork defect was frame 5's buttes reading as one silhouette stamped five times. The cause was the kit, which scaled one shape by height for every seed. Commit 11db5c0.

Notes

Carousel no. 39 shipped at the round cap at 7.428 after five scoring rounds (7.108, 7.2, 7.31, 7.394, 7.428). Round 1's one hard fail was repaired in round 2: slide 5 and the caption had printed El Paso's 60 day removal as what passed, while the council's own record marks both items approved as revised. The deck and the web edition now give the 60 days as the filed term. After the cap, three frames regained a computed figure so CI's figure_bearing passes: the 60 band rod on 5, the 32 poles behind Kyle's camera on 7, and Laredo's nine votes as dais chairs on 9. The panel did not score those. The record: reverify.py now asks the crawl boundary and each host's live robots.txt before it fetches. It refused 12 urls today, including search.txcourts.gov, which now carries a measured unreachable block on tx-2026-0127. tx-2026-0146, Wiwynn's El Paso County plant, was admitted on Wiwynn's dated copy of the release, so the record now holds 167 items. tx-2026-0174 was corrected so El Paso's terms read as filed. A maintainer should merge the duplicate El Paso records (0147 and 0174) and the duplicate UTSA records (0141 and 0167). Prompt audit, final at Phase 19: exit 1. It counted 541 of 1,544 calls whose permission decision took 1.0 to 11.2 seconds, the longest an Agent call. The no-stall hook was armed at 06:17:01 UTC, judged the session unattended (host CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0), refused nothing and logged no dialog left waiting. No call waited longer than 11.2 seconds and the run never stalled. Seconds long decisions on a third of calls read like an automatic check rather than a person, which is a reading and not established.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
